claim_verdicts.evidence: EventSourcedOrder.cs @ stage-3: "public int LoadedVersion => Version - newEvents.Count;". FromEvents applies stored events via Apply (not Record), so newEvents stays empty after replay and LoadedVersion == Version.

InMemoryEventStore.cs @ stage-3: "Append(order.Id, order.LoadedVersion, order.NewEvents); order.MarkSaved();" and EventSourcedOrder.cs: "public void MarkSaved() => newEvents.Clear();". A throw from Append skips MarkSaved.

InMemoryEventStore.cs lines 25-29 @ stage-3: "if (stream.Count != expectedVersion) throw new StreamConcurrencyException(...); stream.AddRange(events); all.AddRange(events);" — the throw precedes both AddRange calls. Lesson code block matches source (tools/validate exit 0).

EventSourcedOrder.cs @ stage-3: Apply ends with "Version++;" after the switch, for every event type; FromEvents starts from "new EventSourcedOrder()" (Version default 0) and applies each stream event once. So Version after replay = stream.Count.

EventSourcedOrder.cs @ stage-3: Cancel throws only "if (Status is \"cancelled\" or \"shipped\")"; Ship throws "if (Status != \"paid\")"; both then call Record, which calls Apply (Version++) and adds to newEvents, so Version 3, LoadedVersion 3-1 = 2.

EventSourcingTests.cs:40-60 @ stage-3 matches the claim line by line. Executed: dotnet test samples/DonHang.Samples.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~TwoWriters_SecondAppendIsRefused → "Passed!  - Failed: 0, Passed: 1, Skipped: 0, Total: 1".

DonHangDbContext.cs:73-77, marked "lesson: backend.l2.optimistic-concurrency" (that lesson's example_tag is stage-2): "IsRowVersion() on a uint makes the Npgsql provider map Version to PostgreSQL's xmin column"; "e.Property(o => o.Version).IsRowVersion();". Npgsql docs (round-1 WebFetch): "You can map a `uint` property to the PostgreSQL `xmin` system column" with `.IsRowVersion();`.

EF Core concurrency.md: "optimistic concurrency takes no locks"; "in addition to the `PersonId` in the WHERE clause, EF Core has added a condition for `Version` as well". Source comment DonHangDbContext.cs:75-76: "EF Core then adds \"AND xmin = <value it read>\" to the WHERE of every UPDATE of an order."

EventSourcedOrder.cs @ stage-3: Apply only assigns fields in a switch ("case OrderShipped: Status = \"shipped\"; break;") and throws nothing; the comment: "Applying an event only sets fields. It checks no rule and never throws". Last event applied sets Status.

Append compares only stream.Count with expectedVersion; after A's save stream.Count is 3, so Append(5, 3, ...) passes and AddRange appends OrderShipped. writerB.NewEvents is not cleared because Save threw before MarkSaved.

InMemoryEventStore.cs @ stage-3: fields are only "streams" and "all"; Load is "=> EventSourcedOrder.FromEvents(ReadStream(orderId))", Save calls Append then MarkSaved; no lock statement, no lock field, nothing held between calls. The only conditional throw is the version check in Append.

Design reasoning that follows from claims 9-10 (store checks only the version; re-appending would pass and replay would apply OrderShipped after OrderCancelled) and from the source comment "so no change is made on top of a stale state". The lesson shows the reasoning instead of asserting a rule.
